records.source: שִׁ֗יר לַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹתאֶשָּׂ֣א עֵ֭ינַי אֶל־הֶהָרִ֑ים מֵ֝אַ֗יִן יָבֹ֥א עֶזְרִֽי׃
records.gloss: A song for the ascents. I lift up my eyes to the mountains; from where will come my help?
pieces: A song of ascents. \q I look up to the mountains. \q Where will my help come from?

L.1: A song for the ascents. \q I lift up my eyes to the mountains; \q from where will my help come?

R.1: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem. \q I look up at the hills. \q Where can I find help?

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: As in 120:1, the short title and the first line are counted together as verse 1, so the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a song of ascents: probably a pilgrim song
decisions.reason: As in 120:1: one of the fifteen songs probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: for the ascents
decisions.reason: This title alone has "a song for the ascents" (le-ma'alot) rather than "the song of the ascents". The sense is the same; Literal shows the difference.

decisions.choice: a question: from where?
alternatives: a statement: the hills, from where my help comes
decisions.reason: The word (me'ayin) asks "from where?", and verse 2 gives the answer. Older renderings that read it as "from which my help comes" make the hills the source of help, which verse 2 corrects.

decisions.choice: the mountains: the hills on the way to Jerusalem
alternatives: hills of danger and false worship
decisions.reason: A pilgrim on the road sees the hills ahead: the hills around Jerusalem where God's house stands (87:1; 125:2), but also hills where robbers hid and where other gods were worshiped (Jeremiah 3:23). Either way the question is answered in verse 2: help comes from the LORD who made the hills.

decisions.choice: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in 120:1.

records.heading: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} guards your going and coming

records.source: עֶ֭זְרִי מֵעִ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה עֹ֝שֵׂ֗ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: My help [is] from with YHWH, maker of heaven and earth.
pieces: My help is from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q the one who made heaven and earth.

L.2: My help [is] from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q maker of heaven and earth.

R.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is the one who helps me. \q He made the heavens and the earth.

decisions.choice: from with: from the presence of
decisions.reason: The double preposition (me'im) means "from beside" or "from the presence of": help comes from where the LORD is.

decisions.choice: maker of heaven and earth: the creator of all
decisions.reason: The LORD is named as the one who made everything (Genesis 1:1; 14:19). Help from the creator of the whole world is greater than any help the hills, or anything in them, could give. The same words close 124:8 and 134:3 and appear in 115:15.

records.gloss: Not may he give to slip your foot; not may he slumber, your keeper.
pieces: May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} never let your foot stumble; \q may the one who guards you never doze.

L.3: May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not allow your foot to slip; \q may your keeper not slumber.

R.3: May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keep you from falling. \q May the one who protects you stay awake.

decisions.choice: a wish: may he not ...
decisions.reason: The negative used here ('al) usually goes with a wish or a request, "may he not". A second voice seems to speak to the pilgrim, blessing him; verse 4 then answers the wish with a firm "he will not" (lo'). Many read verse 3 as a promise already.

decisions.choice: your foot slip: a fall, disaster
decisions.reason: A slipping foot is a picture of falling into trouble (38:17; 66:9), and on a mountain road it is also a real danger.

decisions.choice: your: one person addressed
decisions.reason: From here on the psalm speaks to "you" (singular): another voice, perhaps a priest or a fellow pilgrim, answers the one who spoke in verses 1-2, or the psalmist speaks to himself.

decisions.choice: keep (L); guard (B); protect (R)
decisions.reason: The verb shamar comes six times in this psalm (verses 3-8). Each level keeps one English word for it throughout, so that the repetition, which carries the psalm, can be heard.

records.source: הִנֵּ֣ה לֹֽא־יָ֭נוּם וְלֹ֣א יִישָׁ֑ן שׁ֝וֹמֵ֗ר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Look, not he will slumber and not he will sleep, [the] keeper of Israel.
pieces: Indeed, the one who guards Israel \q never dozes off and never sleeps.

L.4: Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not slumber and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not sleep, \q the keeper of Israel.

R.4: The one who protects Israel never gets sleepy. \q He never sleeps.

decisions.choice: look, he will not: the answer to the wish
decisions.reason: "Look" (hinneh) points to something certain. What verse 3 wished ("may he not slumber") is now stated as fact with the plain negative (lo').

decisions.choice: a God who does not sleep
decisions.reason: Elijah mocked Baal as a god who might be asleep (1 Kings 18:27); the God of Israel never needs to be woken. When the psalms call on God to wake up (44:24), they speak as people who feel forgotten, not of a God who sleeps.

decisions.choice: keep (L); guard (B); protect (R)
decisions.reason: As in 121:3.

records.source: יְהוָ֥ה שֹׁמְרֶ֑ךָ יְהוָ֥ה צִ֝לְּךָ֗ עַל־יַ֥ד יְמִינֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: YHWH [is] your keeper; YHWH [is] your shade at [the] hand of your right.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is the one who guards you; \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is shade at your right side.

L.5: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] your keeper; \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} [is] your shade at your right hand.

R.5: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} protects you. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} stands next to you like shade that keeps off the heat.

decisions.choice: shade: protection from the burning sun
decisions.reason: In a hot land, shade means relief and safety (Isaiah 25:4; 32:2). The picture leads into verse 6.

decisions.choice: at your right hand: close beside you
decisions.reason: The right side is where a helper or defender stands (16:8; 109:31; 110:5).

decisions.choice: keep (L); guard (B); protect (R)
decisions.reason: As in 121:3.

decisions.choice: stands next to you like shade that keeps off the heat
alternatives: your shade at your right hand
decisions.reason: Readable explains both pictures (m1, m2).

records.gloss: By day the sun not will strike you, and [the] moon by night.
pieces: By day the sun will not beat down on you, \q and by night the moon will do you no harm.

L.6: By day the sun will not strike you, \q nor the moon by night.

R.6: The sun will not hurt you during the day. \q The moon will not hurt you at night.

decisions.choice: the sun strike you: sunstroke
decisions.reason: The heat of the sun could strike a traveler down (2 Kings 4:18-20; Jonah 4:8; Isaiah 49:10).

decisions.choice: the moon: dangers of the night
decisions.reason: People of the time believed that the moon could cause illness, and the night was a time of danger. Day and night together mean all the time: no hour is outside the LORD's care.

records.gloss: YHWH will keep you from all evil; he will keep your soul.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will guard you against every harm; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will guard your very life.

L.7: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will keep you from all evil; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will keep your soul.

R.7: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will protect you from every danger. \q He will protect your life.

decisions.choice: evil: harm, disaster
decisions.reason: The word (ra') covers both wrongdoing and the harm that comes on a person. Here it is harm and disaster of every kind.

decisions.choice: your soul (L); your life (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life", since the word means the whole living person.

decisions.choice: keep (L); guard (B); protect (R)
decisions.reason: As in 121:3.

records.gloss: YHWH will keep your going out and your coming in from now and until forever.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will guard you as you set out and as you return, \q from now on and for all time.

L.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will keep your going out and your coming in \q from now and until forever.

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will protect you when you leave home and when you come back, \q now and forever.

decisions.choice: going out and coming in: all you do
alternatives: the pilgrim's journey there and back
decisions.reason: Going out and coming in is a way of saying all of life's activity, everywhere one goes (Deuteronomy 28:6; 1 Samuel 29:6). For a pilgrim it also fits the journey to Jerusalem and home again.

decisions.choice: keep (L); guard (B); protect (R)
decisions.reason: As in 121:3.

decisions.choice: when you leave home and when you come back
alternatives: your going out and your coming in
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain sense of the pair (m1).
